symptoms.symptom: Refrigerator does not operate

causes.label: Refrigerator in defrost cycle.
remedies: Wait about 30 minutes for defrost cycle to end.
Move the freezer control to a temperature setting.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Refrigerator in defrost cycle."

causes.label: Freezer control in 0 (off) position.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Freezer control in 0 (off) position."

causes.label: Refrigerator is unplugged.
remedies: Push the plug completely into the outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Refrigerator is unplugged."

causes.label: The fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset the breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped."

symptoms.symptom: Vibration or rattling (slight vibration is normal)

causes.label: Front rollers need adjusting.
remedies: See Rollers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Front rollers need adjusting."

symptoms.symptom: Motor operates for long periods or cycles on and off frequently. (Modern refrigerators with more storage space and a larger freezer require more operating time. They start and stop often to maintain even temperatures.)

causes.label: Normal when refrigerator is first plugged in.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Normal when refrigerator is first plugged in."

causes.label: Often occurs when large amounts of food are placed in refrigerator.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Often occurs when large amounts of food are placed in refrigerator."

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Door left open."

causes.label: Hot weather or frequent door openings.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Hot weather or frequent door openings."

causes.label: Temperature controls set at the coldest setting.
remedies: See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Temperature controls set at the coldest setting."

symptoms.symptom: Fresh food or freezer compartment too warm

causes.label: Temperature control not set cold enough.
remedies: See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Temperature control not set cold enough."

causes.label: Warm weather or frequent door openings.
remedies: Set the temperature control one step colder.
See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Warm weather or frequent door openings."

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Door left open."

symptoms.symptom: Frost or ice crystals on frozen food (frost within package is normal)

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Door left open."

causes.label: Too frequent or too long door openings.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Too frequent or too long door openings."

symptoms.symptom: Divider between fresh food and freezer compartments feels warm

causes.label: Automatic energy saver system circulates warm liquid around front edge of freezer compartment.
remedies: This helps prevent condensation on the outside.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Automatic energy saver system circulates warm liquid around front edge of freezer compartment."

symptoms.symptom: Automatic icemaker does not work (on some models)

causes.label: Icemaker power switch is in the O (off) position.
remedies: Set the power switch to the l (on) position.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Icemaker power switch is in the O (off) position."

causes.label: Water supply turned off or not connected.
remedies: See Installing the water line.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Water supply turned off or not connected."

causes.label: Freezer compartment too warm.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Freezer compartment too warm."

causes.label: Piled up cubes in the storage bin cause the icemaker to shut off.
remedies: Level cubes by hand.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Piled up cubes in the storage bin cause the icemaker to shut off."

causes.label: Ice cubes stuck in icemaker. (Green power light on icemaker blinking).
remedies: Turn off the icemaker, remove cubes, and turn the icemaker back on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Ice cubes stuck in icemaker. (Green power light on icemaker blinking)."

symptoms.symptom: Ice cubes have odor/taste

causes.label: Ice storage bin needs cleaning.
remedies: Empty and wash bin.
Discard old cubes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Ice storage bin needs cleaning."

causes.label: Food transmitting odor/taste to ice cubes.
remedies: Wrap foods well.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Food transmitting odor/taste to ice cubes."

causes.label: Interior of refrigerator needs cleaning.
remedies: See Care and cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Interior of refrigerator needs cleaning."

symptoms.symptom: Small or hollow cubes

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge with new cartridge or with plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Water filter clogged."

symptoms.symptom: Slow ice cube freezing

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Door left open."

causes.label: Temperature control not set cold enough.
remedies: See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Temperature control not set cold enough."

symptoms.symptom: Door not closing properly

causes.label: Door gasket on hinge side sticking or folding over.
remedies: Apply petroleum jelly on face of gasket.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Door gasket on hinge side sticking or folding over."

symptoms.symptom: Orange glow in the freezer

causes.label: Defrost heater is on.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Defrost heater is on."

symptoms.symptom: Cube dispenser does not work (on some models)

causes.label: Icemaker turned off or water supply turned off.
remedies: Turn on icemaker or water supply.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Icemaker turned off or water supply turned off."

causes.label: Ice cubes are frozen to icemaker feeler arm.
remedies: Remove cubes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Ice cubes are frozen to icemaker feeler arm."

causes.label: Irregular ice clumps in storage container.
remedies: Break up with fingertip pressure and discard remaining clumps. •Freezer may be too warm.
Adjust the freezer control to a colder setting, one position at a time, until clumps do not form.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Irregular ice clumps in storage container."

causes.label: Dispenser is LOCKED.
remedies: Press and hold the LOCK CONTROL pad for 3 seconds.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Dispenser is LOCKED."

symptoms.symptom: Water has poor taste/odor (on some models)

causes.label: Water dispenser has not been used for a long time.
remedies: Dispense water until all water in system is replenished.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water dispenser has not been used for a long time."

symptoms.symptom: Water in first glass is warm (on some models)

causes.label: Normal when refrigerator is first installed.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Normal when refrigerator is first installed."

causes.label: Water dispenser has not been used for a long time.
remedies: Dispense water until all water in system is replenished.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water dispenser has not been used for a long time."

causes.label: Water system has been drained.
remedies: Allow several hours for replenished supply to chill.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water system has been drained."

symptoms.symptom: Water dispenser does not work (on some models)

causes.label: Water supply line turned off or not connected.
remedies: See Installing the water line.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water supply line turned off or not connected."

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge or remove filter and install plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water filter clogged."

causes.label: Air may be trapped in the water system.
remedies: Press the dispenser arm for at least two minutes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Air may be trapped in the water system."

causes.label: Dispenser is LOCKED.
remedies: Press and hold the LOCK CONTROL pad for 3 seconds.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Dispenser is LOCKED."

symptoms.symptom: Water spurting from dispenser

causes.label: Newly-installed filter cartridge.
remedies: Run water from the dispenser for 3 minutes (about one and a half gallons).

symptoms.symptom: Water is not dispensed but icemaker is working

causes.label: Water in reservoir is frozen.
remedies: Call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water in reservoir is frozen."

symptoms.symptom: No water or ice cube production

causes.label: Supply line or shutoff valve is clogged.
remedies: Call a plumber.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Supply line or shutoff valve is clogged."

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge or remove filter and install plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Water filter clogged."

causes.label: Dispenser is LOCKED.
remedies: Press and hold the LOCK CONTROL pad for 3 seconds.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Dispenser is LOCKED."

remedies: Foods with strong odors should be tightly wrapped.
Keep an open box of baking soda in the refrigerator; replace every three months.

remedies: See Care and cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Interior needs cleaning."

remedies: See Care and cleaning.

causes.label: Too frequent or too long door openings.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "Too frequent or too long door openings."

symptoms.symptom: Interior light does not work

causes.label: No power at outlet.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset the breaker.

remedies: See Replacing the light bulbs.
